rv.q: This play is a must see, maybe twice, you're bound to miss something.
Marie Antoinette and the Magical Negroes is one of those plays that I am positive will stick with me for a long time.
This is a brilliant debut that uses comedy to give meaning to the absurdity of any ruling class.
It’s a smart, dizzying show that feels particularly urgent now.

Still, he fails to strike a meaningful chord that will have people contemplating their past harmful conduct or cause them to leave reflecting on how their future intersections with people of color will change after seeing this performance.
The Story Theatre, in its second season, has mounted a theatrical feast with Marie Antoinette and The Magical Negroes .
Although I do not prefer a story that focuses on dehumanizing others on stage, this show is nevertheless intriguing.

cn.t: Critics are sharply divided on this provocative political satire, with most praising Guest's bold direction and the cast's performances, though some find the violent imagery revolting and the ambitious historical mashup uneven.
